name: Christopher Lee
description:
'''Sir Christopher Frank Carandini Lee''' (27 May 1922 – 7 June 2015) was an English actor and singer. In a career spanning over 60 years, he became known as an actor with tremendous screen presence and a deep and commanding voice, who often portrayed villains in horror and franchise films. Lee was [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] for services to drama and charity in June 2009, and received the [[BAFTA Fellowship]] in 2011 and the [[British Film Institute Fellowship|BFI Fellowship]] in 2013.

After playing smaller roles in films like ''[[Corridor of Mirrors (film)|Corridor of Mirrors]]'' (1948), ''[[Captain Horatio Hornblower]]'' (1951), ''[[Moulin Rouge (1952 film)|Moulin Rouge]]'' (1952), ''[[Bitter Victory]]'' (1957), and ''[[A Tale of Two Cities (1958 film)|A Tale of Two Cities]]'' (1958), Lee gained fame for portraying [[Count Dracula]] in seven [[Hammer Film Productions|Hammer Horror]] films, beginning with ''[[Dracula (1958 film)|Dracula]]'' (1958). A fixture of Hammer films, he starred in ''[[Taste of Fear]]'' (1961), ''[[Rasputin the Mad Monk]]'' (1966), ''[[The Devil Rides Out (film)|The Devil Rides Out]]'' (1968), ''[[To the Devil a Daughter]]'' (1976), and opposite his friend [[Peter Cushing]] in ''[[The Curse of Frankenstein]]'' (1957), ''[[The Hound of the Baskervilles (1959 film)|The Hound of the Baskervilles]]'' (1959), ''[[The Mummy (1959 film)|The Mummy]]'' (1959), and ''[[The Gorgon]]'' (1964). He also starred in other horror films, such as ''[[The City of the Dead (film)|The City of the Dead]]'' (1960), ''[[The Whip and the Body]]'' (1963), ''[[Castle of the Living Dead]]'' (1964), ''[[Dr. Terror's House of Horrors]]'' (1965), ''[[Eugenie... The Story of Her Journey into Perversion|Eugenie]]'' (1969), ''[[The House That Dripped Blood]]'' (1971), ''[[Horror Express]]'' (1972), and ''[[Death Line]]'' (1972).

Lee received praise for his performances as Lord Summerisle in ''[[The Wicker Man]]'' (1973) and [[Francisco Scaramanga]] in the [[Production of the James Bond films|James Bond film]] ''[[The Man with the Golden Gun (film)|The Man with the Golden Gun]]'' (1974). He returned to prominence with a new generation of audiences for his roles as [[Saruman]] in [[The Lord of the Rings (film series)|''The Lord of the Rings'' film trilogy]] (2001–2003), which he reprised in [[The Hobbit (film series)|''The Hobbit'' film trilogy]] (2012–2014), and as [[Count Dooku]] in ''[[Star Wars: Episode II – Attack of the Clones]]'' (2002) and ''[[Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Sith]]'' (2005). Around this time, he became a [[List of frequent Tim Burton collaborators|frequent collaborator]] of [[Tim Burton]], appearing in his films ''[[Sleepy Hollow (film)|Sleepy Hollow]]'' (1999), ''[[Corpse Bride]]'' (2005), ''[[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory (film)|Charlie and the Chocolate Factory]]'' (2005), ''[[Alice in Wonderland (2010 film)|Alice in Wonderland]]'' (2010), and ''[[Dark Shadows (film)|Dark Shadows]]'' (2012). Other notable film credits include ''[[The Three Musketeers (1973 live-action film)|The Three Musketeers]]'' (1973), ''[[Airport '77]]'' (1977), ''[[The Last Unicorn (film)|The Last Unicorn]]'' (1982), ''[[Gremlins 2: The New Batch]]'' (1990), ''[[Jinnah (film)|Jinnah]]'' (1998), and ''[[Hugo (film)|Hugo]]'' (2011).

Lee was also a classically trained singer with a passion for [[Heavy metal music|heavy metal]]. He recorded several albums, including the symphonic-metal concept albums ''[[Charlemagne: By the Sword and the Cross]]'' (2010) and ''[[Charlemagne: The Omens of Death]]'' (2013), portraying the title character of Charlemagne. These projects featured Lee providing spoken word, singing, and dramatic narration.
